Name: Ingest Reported Data
What Happens: System receives the reported data submitted under a regulatory framework (e.g., data reported to comply with FR 2590 Single-Counterparty Credit Limits) with ~20 reportable line items. Each line item represents a reported value that must be validated against source evidence. The FR 2590 instruction manual itself serves as regulatory context (how values should be calculated) — it is not the data being tested.
Implementation: Python — automated ingestion triggered by reporting calendar or analyst submission
GS Enterprise Integration: Connects to GS regulatory reporting platform (e.g., AxiomSL, Moody's). Could also accept manual upload from analyst. Scheduled trigger aligned to reporting deadlines.
Data Sources / Inputs: Sample summary file (the reported values GS submitted), reporting calendar, line item metadata (schedule, counterparty, product type). Separately: FR 2590 instruction manual as regulatory PDF context for Phases 4-5.
Output: Structured list of LineItem objects — each with unique ID, reported value, attributes, metadata (currency, product type, counterparty, schedule)
Guardrail: Validate line item count against expected schedule. Flag missing or malformed items before processing begins.
Human Touchpoint: Analyst confirms the filing is ready for validation

Name: Associate Transactional Documents
What Happens: For each line item, identify and retrieve the unique transactional source documents needed to validate the reported value. Fan out: each line item spawns its own independent processing thread.
Implementation: Python + LangGraph fan-out via Send() API. Each line item gets its own parallel subgraph running Phases 3-6 independently.
GS Enterprise Integration: Retrieves documents from GS document management systems: DocLake, S3 evidence stores, trade capture systems (SecDB, Marquee), risk platforms. Document-to-line-item association could be rule-based (trade ID lookup) or metadata-driven.
Data Sources / Inputs: Trade confirmations (from booking systems), market data (Bloomberg, Reuters), FX rates (Treasury), collateral positions (margin systems), interest accruals (accounting systems), counterparty records (KYC/PHUB)
Output: Per-line-item document package — scoped set of source evidence files relevant to that specific line item
Guardrail: Flag line items with zero associated documents. Validate document freshness (not stale/outdated). Verify document authenticity metadata.
Human Touchpoint: Analyst reviews flagged items where documents could not be auto-associated

Name: Classify Source Type
What Happens: For each document in the line item's package, determine the extraction approach: structured (Excel/CSV), image (screenshot/scan), or unstructured (PDF text, email, legal doc).
Implementation: Python — content-based classification. Inspect file content, not just extension. PDFs: test text extractability. Excel: verify parseable headers.
GS Enterprise Integration: Classification rules can be pre-configured per document source system (e.g., SecDB always produces structured Excel, PHUB screenshots are always image). Override capability for edge cases.
Data Sources / Inputs: Document bytes, file metadata, source system tags
Output: Classification label per document: structured / image / unstructured. Routes to appropriate extraction agent in Phase 4-5.
Guardrail: Log classification decision with rationale. If ambiguous, attempt multiple extraction methods and compare. Alert if a document type has never been seen before.
Human Touchpoint: None — automated unless ambiguous classification triggers alert

Name: Identify Data Needed
What Happens: For each line item, determine what specific data points are required to validate the reported value. Produces a 'data requirements manifest' scoping extraction before it begins.
Implementation: LLM call within per-line-item subgraph. Uses regulatory instruction manual + line item metadata to derive requirements.
GS Enterprise Integration: References GS-maintained regulatory data dictionaries and FR 2590 instruction manual. Could integrate with existing data lineage tools to auto-suggest data sources.
Data Sources / Inputs: Line item attributes, document previews (headers/schema), FR 2590 instruction manual, GS data dictionaries
Output: Data requirements manifest: for each attribute, what data is needed, from which document, what relationship (direct lookup, filtered lookup, cross-source calculation)
Guardrail: Validate every reportable attribute has at least one identified data source. Flag gaps immediately — do not proceed to mapping with unresolvable attributes.
Human Touchpoint: Analyst reviews any attributes where no data source could be identified

Name: Map Data to Documents
What Happens: LLM maps each identified data point to its exact location in the source documents — specific column, row-matching logic (join keys), transformation rules, cross-source formulas.
Implementation: LLM call with confidence scoring. Updated prompt requires HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW confidence per mapping with rationale.
GS Enterprise Integration: Mapping results stored in GS audit system for regulatory traceability. Historical mappings from prior reporting periods can be provided as context to improve accuracy and consistency.
Data Sources / Inputs: Data requirements manifest (Phase 4), document content previews, historical mapping results from prior periods, regulatory PDF context
Output: Column mappings with confidence scores: join keys, source labels, source columns, transformation types, cross-source formulas
Guardrail: HIGH confidence (>90%): proceed automatically. MEDIUM (60-90%): proceed but flag in report. LOW (<60%): pause and surface to analyst for review.
Human Touchpoint: KEY TOUCHPOINT: Analyst reviews LOW confidence mappings. Options: confirm, edit, provide context, or skip. Every override logged for audit trail.

Name: Testing Comparison
What Happens: Programmatic comparison engine executes all mappings: resolves source values via join keys or filtered lookups, evaluates cross-source formulas, compares reported vs. source, calculates variance.
Implementation: Python — deterministic engine. No LLM involvement. Safe ast.parse for formulas. Tolerance-based comparison for FX rounding. Handles 6+ date formats, Unicode normalization.
GS Enterprise Integration: Results written to GS testing evidence database. Each comparison linked to source document, line item, and mapping for full audit traceability. Integrates with existing exception management workflows.
Data Sources / Inputs: Mapped source documents (Phase 5), reported values (Phase 1), comparison tolerance thresholds (configurable per product/attribute)
Output: Per-line-item comparison results: Pass/Fail/Pending per attribute with variance amount, source value, reported value, source document reference
Guardrail: Flag line items with >50% failure rate — may indicate systemic mapping error rather than genuine data issues. Tolerance thresholds configurable per attribute type.
Human Touchpoint: None — fully automated. Failures surface in Phase 7 report for analyst review.

Name: Report Generation + Review
What Happens: Fan-in: aggregate results from all parallel line item subgraphs. Generate consolidated audit report with full traceability. Route to appropriate reviewer.
Implementation: Python + LLM formatting. Fan-in via LangGraph. Completeness validation ensures no line items dropped during parallel processing.
GS Enterprise Integration: Report delivered to GS regulatory review workflow. Integrates with existing sign-off/attestation process. Findings routed to appropriate business line for remediation. Report archived for examiner access.
Data Sources / Inputs: All per-line-item comparison results (Phase 6), confidence annotations (Phase 5), analyst overrides log
Output: Consolidated audit report: overall summary (pass/fail/pending counts), per-line-item detail sections, confidence annotations, analyst override audit trail, source document references
Guardrail: Verify all line items from Phase 1 have results (none dropped). Distinguish auto-confirmed vs. human-reviewed mappings. Flag unresolved items requiring manual follow-up.
Human Touchpoint: Analyst reviews full report. Signs off on findings. Escalates failures to business line owners. Report submitted as part of regulatory attestation.
